CoDa Stereo

Compositional Data Analysis for Stereological, Histomorphometric and Blood-Cell Data

A Shiny application implementing the Aitchison geometry for the full data analysis cycle: data upload, zero/NA handling, compositional visualisation, balances, and permutational MANOVA with post-hoc tests. Interface in English, Portuguese and Spanish.

Developed alongside: Provete, D.B., Severgnini, M.R., Fernandes, C.E. & Franco-Belussi, L. A Practical Guide to using Compositional Data Analysis in Tissue Stereology and Blood Cell Profile. Physiological Reports (in review).

Use it online, no installation needed: https://sxzbf8.short.gy/CoDaStereo (the interface opens in English; add ?lang=pt or ?lang=es to the link for Portuguese or Spanish).

See NEWS.md for the changes in each version and the package website for the getting-started guide.

Features

Module Capabilities
Data Upload CSV and Excel (.xlsx/.xls) with sheet selector; the four case-study datasets of the companion paper as examples; aggregation of fields of view into specimens (nested designs); smart parts selector; pre-flight check
Data Inspection Zero/NA heatmap (observed vs. structural zero vs. missing); naniar::vis_miss plot; counts per part
Zero Handling Three methods via zCompositions: CZM (count zeros), multRepl (rounded zeros), lrEM (rounded zeros); NA handling via listwise deletion or geometric-mean imputation
Compositional Analysis Ternary plot in pure ggplot2 with amalgamation, convex hulls or 95% confidence/predictive regions and group centres; clr-biplot on unscaled clr coordinates (axis choice, shapes, labels, optional log-total as in a T-space biplot) with a “how to read” note, scree plot and ray lengths; variation-matrix heatmap; compositional centre and total variance per group; colour palettes (Okabe-Ito, Dark2, viridis); interactive hover (ggiraph)
Balances (SBP) Automatic sequential binary partition (Ward clustering on clr distances), editable cell by cell with on-the-fly validation; CoDa dendrogram; boxplots and permutational tests (Z, P) of each balance by group
Statistical Modeling Permutational MANOVA via RRPP::lm.rrpp with factors, covariates (ANCOVA), a block term, SS type I/II/III and 199-9999 permutations (fixed seed); the log-total as a joint response or a covariate (Pawlowsky-Glahn, Egozcue & Lovell 2015), with a warning when totals are fixed by design; pairwise tests of means and dispersions; residual diagnostics. Fits run in background workers (mirai)
Reproducibility R script that reproduces the analysis; self-contained HTML report; save and reload the session (JSON)
Downloads Every figure as PDF, PNG, SVG or TIFF at a chosen size, resolution and font size; imputed data, SBP, variation matrix, ANOVA, balance and pairwise tables as CSV

Installation

Run locally (recommended for development) 

# Install from GitHub
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("diogoprov/CoDaStereo")

# Launch
CoDaStereo::run_app()

Run without installing (quick start) 

# Clone the repo, then:
setwd("CoDaStereo/")
pkgload::load_all()
run_app()

Dependencies

CoDaStereo depends on: shiny, shinydashboard, rintrojs, dplyr, tidyr, tibble, purrr, ggplot2, ggiraph, ggrepel, scales, svglite, readxl, naniar, compositions, zCompositions, RRPP, FactoMineR, mirai, htmltools, jsonlite, knitr, golem, rlang.

All are available on CRAN.

Deploy to Posit Connect Cloud (free)

Connect Cloud is Posit’s next-generation hosting platform. It deploys directly from a public GitHub repository with automatic push-to-publish.

Step-by-step

  1. Fork or push this repository to your GitHub account.

  2. Generate manifest.json — this file tells Connect Cloud which R version and packages to use. Run this once in your local R session (from the repository root):

    # install.packages("rsconnect")
# list only the files the deployed app needs
f <- system("git ls-files", intern = TRUE)
f <- f[grepl("^(app[.]R|DESCRIPTION|NAMESPACE|LICENSE|R/|www/|inst/)", f)]
rsconnect::writeManifest(appDir = ".", appFiles = f, appPrimaryDoc = "app.R")
# (the same code is in dev/write_manifest.R)

    Commit and push the generated manifest.json.

  3. Sign in to Connect Cloud with your GitHub account.

  4. Click “Publish” (+ icon at the top), select your repository and branch (main). Connect Cloud will detect app.R and deploy automatically.

  5. Get a shareable URL — share it in your manuscript or supplementary materials.

Updating the app

After the initial setup, every git push to main triggers an automatic re-deploy. No manual steps needed.

Alternative: deploy from RStudio 

# One-time authentication (opens browser)
rsconnect::connectCloudUser()

# Deploy
rsconnect::deployApp(appDir = ".", appName = "CoDaStereo")

│   ├── mod_analysis.R     # Ternary, biplot, variation matrix, descriptives
│   ├── mod_balances.R     # SBP editor, CoDa dendrogram, balance tests

Why “CoDa Stereo”?

The name joins the two fields that the package brings together: CoDa, the usual abbreviation of compositional data analysis, and stereology, the quantification of tissue structure whose volume fractions and point counts are compositions by construction. It is also a double musical homage. Coda (1982) is the ninth and final studio album by Led Zeppelin, released almost two years after the band broke up following the death of drummer John Bonham, and its title refers to the closing section of a piece of music. Soda Stereo is the band formed in Buenos Aires in 1982 by Gustavo Cerati, Zeta Bosio and Charly Alberti, regarded as a pioneer of Latin American rock. Changing a single letter turns Soda Stereo into CoDa Stereo.

The logo carries both references in its typography. “CODA” is set in Ryga, a free display typeface with neon-like outlined strokes, chosen as a homage to Led Zeppelin’s Coda. “STEREO” is set in Inter Bold, widely spaced, as a solid 1980s nod to Soda Stereo. Above the name, an isometric block of tissue with cells and blood vessels stands for the object of stereology, and its stacked bars stand both for the parts of a composition and for the level meters of a stereo equalizer. The package has no connection with either band, and the logo uses none of their artwork or lyrics. The fonts are documented in inst/logo/FONTS.md.

How to cite

If you use CoDaStereo in your research, please cite both the paper and the software:

@article{provete2026codastreo,
  author  = {Provete, Diogo B. and Severgnini, Marcos R. and Fernandes, Carlos E. and Franco-Belussi, Lilian},
  title   = {A Practical Guide to using Compositional Data Analysis in Tissue Stereology and Blood Cell Profile},
  journal = {Physiological Reports},
  year    = {2026},
  note    = {In review}
}

@software{provete2026codastreo_app,
  author  = {Provete, Diogo B.},
  title   = {{CoDa Stereo}: Compositional Data Analysis for Stereological Data},
  year    = {2026},
  url     = {https://github.com/diogoprov/CoDaStereo},
  doi     = {10.5281/zenodo.19925778},
  version = {3.1.1}
}
